tldr: Both charge a base seat fee plus separate per-resolution AI billing, and both draw the exact same top complaint in independent reviews: unpredictable AI costs once resolution volume scales past what you budgeted.
Intercom is cheaper to start ($29/seat/mo) and its standalone Fin AI Agent can be deployed onto an existing helpdesk without migrating seats — the faster path to testing AI resolution quality.

Zendesk doesn't unlock AI Agents until the $55/agent/mo Suite Team tier, but once there it offers deeper ticket routing, skills-based assignment, and Admin Copilot for human agents that Intercom doesn't match.
Zendesk's Ease of Setup is its lowest-scoring metric in independent review data; Intercom's standalone Fin deployment is specifically designed to be a faster bolt-on.
Pick Intercom for a faster AI-first deployment with strong conversational quality; pick Zendesk if you need mature omnichannel ticketing and routing at scale and can absorb a steeper learning curve.

Crisp's own head-to-head on this exact matchup (published on their comparisons hub) calls Zendesk's interface 'somewhat dated compared to Intercom' and gives Intercom the edge on video/co-browsing and load time, while conceding Zendesk 'excels at automation and ticketing in more complicated service environments' — a competitor's framing, but it lines up with the conversational-vs-structured split independent reviews show here too.

Neither platform is meaningfully cheaper once you count the whole bill: Intercom's edge is a lower seat price at the AI-enabled entry tier ($29 vs Zendesk needing $55/agent before AI Agents even unlock), but both charge per-resolution on top, so the sticker price on either pricing page understates what you'll actually pay at real support volume.
verdict: This comes down to how fast you need to move and how much ticketing depth you actually need — not which platform is cheaper, because once you add per-resolution AI billing to both, sticker price stops being the deciding factor. Intercom's standalone Fin deployment lets you test AI resolution quality against your existing helpdesk before committing to anything, and its conversational AI has the stronger independent reputation for holding context through a multi-step conversation without losing the thread. Zendesk asks for more up front — you're not touching AI Agents until $55/agent/mo, a full $26 more per seat than Intercom's entry price — but once you're past that line, the routing, skills-based assignment, and Admin Copilot are genuinely built for support orgs juggling five channels and dozens of agents, not a chat widget with a ticketing system bolted on. Crisp's own comparison of this exact matchup (they sell to the same market from underneath both of them) calls Zendesk's interface 'somewhat dated compared to Intercom' while noting Zendesk 'excels at automation and ticketing in more complicated service environments' — a competitor's take, but it lines up with the same conversational-vs-structured split that shows up in independent reviews here. Both platforms share the same real weakness regardless of which you pick: per-resolution AI billing that's genuinely hard to forecast, so get a resolution-cost estimate in writing from either vendor before you sign, not after the first invoice teaches you the hard way.
